President Dropato Munmu has said that the nationwide Beti Bachao Beti Parao campaign has proved
to an important milestone in promoting women's empowerment.
The campaign was launched from Pani Perth in Haryana in January 2015.
She highlighted that the child's sex ratio at birth, which stood at 871 girls per 1000
and boys in 2014 has increased to around 915 in November 2025.
President Moon Moos said this while addressing the state-level Haryana Day celebrations in
Kurukshetra marking the 60th anniversary of the formation of Haryana.
She said that Haryana has made remarkable progress over the past decade in various
dimensions of women's empowerment.
Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, and World Championships.
to the flagged off the Bengaluru Mumbai Bande Bharat sleeper train at Sir M. Vishwesh Swaraya
terminal in Bengaluru, Karnataka, you know, Mr. Sprathas Joshi H.D. Kumaraswamy, Shobha
Karanlaje and V. Sumanna also present on the occasion. Speaking at the event, Mr.
Vaishnav said that the train will seamlessly connect India's IT and startup hub with
this financial capital. The 16-coach Bengaluru Mumbai Sleeper Mandibhara train will cover
the journey between the two cities in around 16 hours. The train will run 6 days a week
except one days from Bengaluru and two days from Mumbai. It will stop at Anantapur,
Guntkal, Rajchur, Yadgir, Kalburgi, Solapur, Pune and Kalyan. Mr. Vaishnav said this
route covers parts of northern Karnataka that were previously unserved by a world
class train. Mr. Vaishnav also said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has approved the Bullet
Train South Corridor for Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Amravati and Chennai. He added that once completed
travel time from Bengaluru to Chennai will be 73 minutes.
The Centre has released additional installment of TAX devolution to the state governments
amounting to Rs.1,919 crore rupees yesterday, which is in addition to the regular
monthly devolution. This is the second additional installment in this financial
year. Finance Ministry said this release is in view of the upcoming festive
season and to enable states to accelerate capital spending and also to
finance the development and welfare related expenditure. Uttar Pradesh has
been given 19,208 crore rupees while 10,845 crore rupees has been
released for Bihar. Madhya Pradesh has been given 8,010 crore rupees and
and West Bengal 7,866 crore rupees. The centres withdrawn the special additional
excise duty on petrol exports while increasing export levies on diesel and aviation turbine
fuel ATF. According to notifications issued by the Ministry of Finance, under the revised
rates petrol exports will attract no export duty compared to the earlier levy of 2 rupees
50 per litre. The export duty on diesel has been increased from 8 rupees 50 per litre to 11 rupees
50 per litre while the levy on ATF has been raised from 10 rupees 50 per litre to 11 rupees per litre.
The revised rates came as the government continues its fourth nightly review of fuel export duties
in response to fluctuations in international crude oil and refined petroleum product prices.
Aviation turbine fuel ATF prices has been increased by Rs 1,37 per litre and commercial LPG rate
has been increased by Rs 10 per 19 kg cylinder. ATF prices have increased to Rs 138,50 per
litre. From Rs 137 to Rs 12 per litre, with increased price of 19 kg commercial LPG cylinder
has touched 2,820 rupees.
UN Health Minister J.P. Nandha to decriticise Congress party for conducting a rally at the
Ramleela Maidan during the festive season.
Talking to media New Delhi, Mr. Nandha said that the Congress party is attempting to
disrupt normal life, affecting the livelihoods of small shopkeepers and traders in the
national capital during the festive season.
He accused the party of creating an atmosphere of unrest in the country.
Congress and its partners in the INDIA block are holding a rally at Ramli
LaMantana in New Delhi to protest alleged electoral irregularities
demanding the removal of the chief election commissioner. Quad
member nations have reaffirmed the commitment to a free and open Indo
Pacific. US Secretary of State and Foreign Ministers of India, Australia and
Japan met in Atlanta, Georgia yesterday to discuss progress on ongoing
Quad initiatives. We have a report. The Quad joint press release on economic prosperity
and security said that the Quad ministers underscored the importance of economic security
in maintaining global stability and prosperity. They reiterated the absolute necessity to
protect and preserve navigational rights and freedoms in the Strait of Hormuz, the
Red Sea and the Bob Almande Strait in accordance with the international law. The Quad ministers
Ministers highlighted the importance of artificial intelligence and initiatives like PEX, CELICA
to the future of economic growth and expressed their intent to provide over $85 million of
technical and financial assistance to support access to trusted SI superintelligence across
the Indo-Pacific.
The Quad ministers expressed their deep concern about the proliferation of online and cyber
scams that pose a threat to national and international peace and security.
The Kuwait ministers expressed their condolences for those who lost their lives during the flash
floods of 26 August in Nepal.
They recognized India's leading role as the first responder to Nepal's rescue, along
with the significant support to Nepal from all Kuwait countries.
With Subarna's report, Vishal Kumar for Akashwani News, Delhi.
Excellencies have held separate meetings with Russian, Polish and South Korean counterparts
in the U.S., discussing the Ukraine conflict, the situation in West Asia, bilateral ties and
multilateral issues. The meetings took place yesterday on the sidelines of the G-20 foreign
ministers meeting in Atlanta. Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Dr. Jay Shankar
said that the politicization of the energy market is harmful and that the global South
is bearing the burnt of it. The distortion of the energy market, the politicization
of energy flows. This is something which is very harmful. The global south was bearing
the brunt of the energy shortages and that something needs to be done and that this issue
itself must be recognized by the G20. This is Akash Vani giving you the news.

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic
storm and approach the Andhra Pradesh coast.
We have a report.
According to the India Metallurgical Department, the system is moving towards the Andhra Pradesh
coast.
It is expected to cross the coast between Nellur and Arsapur on Tuesday morning.
Wind speeds may reach 100 to 110 km per hour with gusts up to 120 km per hour.
The IMD has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several coastal districts and
over the next three days. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea.
Authorities have urged people in low-lying areas to remain alert and follow official
warnings and safety instructions. Allumurli, Akashwani News, Vijayawada.
Six Indian tourists stranded in Nepal's Dolpa district following heavy snowfall
are being evacuated by helicopter as severe weather has blocked tracking routes in the region.
The group comprising four men and two women were stranded in Dhangari area
of Shea Fox Sando Rural Municipality. According to the Dholpa District Administration Office,
information about the stranded tourists were received on October 31st. The helicopter rescue
operation began on November 1st and is currently underway. Massive protests took place in Europe
yesterday as part of demonstrations driven by the cost of living and deficient public
services with police bracing for potential violence after recent looting and riots.
threats. Germany, France, Portugal and Serbia are among the nations where demonstrations held
on Halloween form a recent wave of ZENZI led marches across the continent. We have a report.
In France, police have fired tear gas to disperse protesters in Paris and Lyon as hundreds
of thousands of young people took to the streets across the country to demand better
education and lower living costs. The demonstration in Paris began peacefully but later turned
violent near the designated end point of the main march. Around 70,000 police
personnel and Jain arms were deployed across France to maintain law and order.
The Interior Ministry said at least 290 people had been arrested nationwide.
Meanwhile in Germany, hooted protesters looted shops in Frankfurt yesterday
following demonstrations by tens of thousands of people demanding improved
education facilities and a reduction in the living cost.
The protests organized by a camp and group were held in 34 cities including Berlin,
Frankfurt and Munich. Around 60 people were arrested on charges including property damage
and assault. In Serbia, a student-led activism helped unseating the country's long-term
leader through the ballot boxes. Similar year-led demonstrations were also reported in other
European countries, including Portugal.
Rupesh Rathor for Akash Vani News.
In Men's Cricket in November 185 for 6-19.1 overs against host New Zealand in the fifth
and final T20 International Hamilton when reports last came in. New Zealand won the toss and

in to the playing 11.
In badminton two-time Olympic medalist BB Sindhu Lakshya Sien will be in action in
the women's and men's singles finals respectively at the high low open in Germany today.
In the women's singles finals, second seed PB Sindhu will face Denmark's Linu Kersfeldt
this evening.
Sindhu secured a place in the title clash after defeating fellow Indian Anmol Kharab 21-13-21-16
in the semifinals.
Meanwhile, the men's singles final Lakshya Sen will take on Indonesia's Jonathan Christie.
In hockey India will face Malaysia in the league stage in counter of the men's Asian
Champions Trophy in Jalandhar Punjab this evening.
The match is scheduled to begin at 7 p.m. Indian time. Both teams remain unbeaten in
the tournament and will be looking to continue the winning run. In other matches
scheduled for today, Korea will take on Bangladesh this afternoon, while China
